notes: RBox revision of a subproperty: removes cfo_of ⊑ works_for, which holds (a company's chief financial officer works for it). New relations cfo_of and works_for, catalogued in the Finance staging file finance-replace-rbox.RELATIONS.md. Replaces the earlier edit on wholly_owned_subsidiary_of ⊑ subsidiary_of, which reviewers flagged as lexical: the phrase 'wholly owned subsidiary' names a kind of subsidiary, so the edit fought the words themselves rather than a property of the relation. Here the two relations share no head word; the subproperty is a fact about what the role involves, like capital_of ⊑ located_in. The propositional queries state the edit in plain words (someone can be a company's chief financial officer without working for it), which avoids stacking 'is it false that ... is not a subproperty'. Instances: Amy Hood (Microsoft's CFO since 2013) and Colette Kress (Nvidia's CFO since 2013); the question asks what follows from the given fact, so it does not turn on whether a model knows them. Yes and no are balanced through phrasing: the direct question asks whether the subproperty holds (yes, then no), the first instance whether the conclusion could fail (no, then yes), the second whether it follows (yes, then no); the cross-lingual queries ask the first instance. Near unrelated asks the same property of the sibling relation 'is the chief executive officer of' into the same super-relation (an over-applied edit would turn its yes to no); far asks a different property of an unrelated relation; references are the logical answers. Review pass 2026-11-12: works_for is now defined as 'is employed by it' only (the officer clause made cfo_of a subproperty by definition), so the subproperty is a fact about the role; works_for is many-valued at one time (a board seat plus a job). Fractional or outsourced CFOs still work for the company they serve. Derived[1] gains 'Given only this' so the stored 'Nvidia's Colette Kress' does not decide the answer. Open: the four-model audit is still pending.
